insights.topic: Verified purchase signal vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Every Crinkl token represents a cryptographically confirmed transaction, not an inferred intent — a structural distinction from cookie-based or behavioral targeting where the industry pays $5+ CPM to guess at purchase likelihood.

Three consecutive heartbeats of rising velocity (0.679x → 0.715x → 0.736x) with zero new geographies added signals that existing users are submitting more receipts — a behavioral deepening, not a recruitment spike.

At 3.099 bits across 15 active categories, basket diversity is near its all-time peak; a basket CV of 0.46 indicates new spend categories are actively entering the dataset, expanding the addressable surface for brand measurement.

insights.topic: Digital and AI-native commerce now verifiable
insights.insight: Ten vendors including Amazon, Stripe, Paddle, and multiple OpenAI endpoints entered the DKIM allowlist in a single burst on May 2 — meaning SaaS, AI subscriptions, and digital marketplace spend can now be verified alongside physical retail.

Seven-day GMV has held in the $80–89K band for multiple consecutive readings, establishing a durable intake baseline rather than episodic volume — the kind of consistency that supports panel-level measurement commitments.

insights.topic: Cost structure vs. ad tech benchmarks
insights.insight: At $0.10 per verified receipt against a $5–$150 CPA range in performance advertising, the unit economics favor verified commerce data by one to three orders of magnitude — relevant as identity deprecation raises the cost of probabilistic alternatives.
